vulnerabilities.description: External CDN dependency for PDF.js worker without Subresource Integrity (SRI). Loading from https://esm.run/ is vulnerable to MITM attacks. Should use SRI hash or serve from own CDN.
Error message from Firebase Auth directly exposed to user in DOM. Error messages may contain sensitive information or stack traces that aid attackers.
Debug logging in production code (console.log). Disable in production to prevent information leakage.
Debug logging in production code (console.log). Disable in production to prevent information leakage.
Client-side error logging with console.error exposes implementation details. Combined with external PDF.js load, this could aid reconnaissance.
Firebase configuration loaded from meta tag without validation. While Firebase config is typically non-sensitive (public API keys), ensure no secrets are accidentally embedded here.
Hidden form fields for CSRF token and auth token sent via POST. Ensure backend validates CSRF token and uses SameSite cookie attributes.
No explicit file type validation before processing. Relies on server-side validation (good), but adding client-side mime type checks would prevent malicious files from being processed client-side.
Third-party Firebase library loaded from external CDN without SRI. Consider pinning specific versions and using SRI hashes.

recommendations: Add Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes to all external CDN resources (PDF.js worker, Firebase libs)
Wrap PDF.js worker URL in a CSP-compliant data URL or serve from same origin to eliminate external dependency
Remove or disable all console.log/console.error statements in production builds using build-time stripping
Sanitize Firebase error messages before displaying: use generic error text, log actual errors server-side only
Ensure all forms use SameSite=Strict cookie attributes and validate CSRF tokens server-side
Add Content Security Policy (CSP) headers to restrict external script/worker loading
Implement client-side file type validation (check magic bytes, not just extensions) before server submission
Validate Firebase config in meta tag format to prevent injection; use JSON.parse with try-catch
Add rate limiting on file processing endpoints (already partially done with authorizeConversion)
Consider implementing file size limits both client and server-side to prevent DoS
Audit all vendor libraries for known CVEs; keep Firebase SDK updated
